A1.justification: Despite the changed title and framing, both PDFs describe the same SCM-based assessment framework and biomedical dataset. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original human annotations, analyses of assessment variability and causal effects, and experiments with four LLMs.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds refinement experiments, human evaluation, an NLP-domain transfer study and a live-assistance pilot.

M1.justification: Section 5 adds verdict-conditioned feedback and refinement after the forward LLM workflow, using previous answers and the encoded graph. v1 uses forward execution without this stage. This substantially changes inference and its inputs; the original biomedical workflow and Gaussian-process SCM fitting remain.

E1.justification: v2 extends actual coverage beyond biomedical assessment: Appendix A.5 reports 33 NLP researchers assessing six NLP papers, and A.2 analyzes 30 NLPEER reviews. It also tests live human–LLM assistance. The original 22-paper biomedical dataset remains; essay scoring is only a proposed application.

E2.justification: The four LLM backbones and human/majority baselines remain. v1's graph-free GPT4o§ comparison corresponds to the unrefined GPT4oγ in v2 Table 14. v2 additionally evaluates a self-refined graph-free GPT-4o comparator, now labeled GPT4o§.

E3.justification: Main-table program F1 changes from majority-vote references to individual annotator references; v2 Table 14 reports both. v2 also adds paper-referenced SummaC and a human-evaluation protocol covering eight workflow steps on three papers, with fact-matching and explanation-alignment judgments. The original 20/2-paper test/development split remains.

E4.justification: v2 adds explicit refinement ablations, leave-one-paper-out stability analysis, paper-grounded factual-alignment analysis and human validation of automatic metrics. The original variability-propagation and graph-removal error analyses are retained, including material relocated to Appendices A.6 and A.7.2.

E5.justification: Targeted statistical additions include leave-one-paper-out t-tests with Bonferroni correction and p-values, plus human–metric correlations. Existing standard deviations across steps and papers remain; additional repeated runs are not documented. The correlation procedure is ambiguously identified as Pearson in A.7.3 and Spearman in Table 16.

E6.justification: Table 14 retains v1's unrefined results and adds refined results, individual-reference F1 and paper-referenced SummaC. Tables 15–16 add human-evaluation outcomes and metric correlations; transfer and assistance studies add survey findings. Main-table numerical differences partly reflect changed procedures and scoring references, so they do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 Definition 1 generalizes v1 Definition 2: inference can concern hidden components or verdicts given partially observed workflow variables, rather than all components given inputs and verdicts. It also explicitly requires input-to-step connectivity. The existing SCM, intervention, counterfactual and ACE mathematics is retained, partly in Appendix A.2.1.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from modeling natural-language diagnostic abduction to specifying a broader family of structured critical-text-assessment problems, with abduction as one experimental setting. The biomedical dataset and principal claims about prior knowledge, writing style, error propagation and human oversight remain.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the rationale for fixed causal workflows and verdict-conditioned assistance, and interprets metric suitability separately for extraction and explanation alignment. It adds explicit limits on comparing annotator groups, using unvalidated NLP-transfer annotations, and generalizing small user-study findings to real human–AI collaboration.

D1.justification: v1 promises code and data upon acceptance; v2 reports public availability and supplies a repository address. v2 also provides complete feedback/refinement prompts in Tables 12–13, graph-encoding details and instructions for populating prompt inputs. Existing model versions, generation settings and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially expanded and repositioned around document-quality assessment, review generation, fact-checking, essay grading and clinical diagnostic assistance. Section 2 and Appendix A.1 add substantive comparisons with these approaches. Much of v1's abductive-reasoning and explainability discussion is retained in the appendix.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and substantial portions of Sections 3–5 are rewritten around STRICTA. Formal causal background and error-propagation discussion move to appendices, a transfer section precedes the conclusion, and the appendix is reorganized with expanded positioning and design discussions.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, v1 Figures 3–4 become the two panels of v2 Figure 3, and a new Figure 4 illustrates diagnosis across domains. Tables 12–16 add prompt displays, expanded experimental comparisons and human-evaluation results. Original workflow graphs and specification tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens experimental relevance and validation: it explicitly implements verdict-conditioned reasoning, preserves unrefined controls, and supplements automatic and simulated evaluation with human metric assessment, live assistance and domain-transfer evidence. Fuller procedural documentation and reported resource release improve reproducibility. These address important gaps in v1, although small pilot samples, unvalidated transfer annotations and the Pearson/Spearman inconsistency limit the strength of the new conclusions.
